composition.serve_who: This sheet ("AFT COMPANION WAY", DWG GMMS 108'-118a) documents the J/BOX enclosure and control loops for the AFT companion-way's INFLATABLE HATCH SEAL (pneumatic gasket) system, matching the engineer mapping AFT COMPANION WAY -> 575-pneumatic-system. All labeled devices (HATCH OPEN/CLOSED indicators S1/S2, digital pressure switch "open when inflated", SW19 open/closed/LOCK selector, inside-locker inflate/deflate switch, V1 inflate/deflate valve, AUX inflate/deflate valve, reed switch closed signal, and the Re1-Re8 relay bank) all serve this one inflatable-seal/hatch-lock system per the sheet's own title and the q48/q49 engineer answers confirming both companionways have an inflatable seal (aft = Likon IFS840425). The FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 pinout (open/LOCK/closed/BOOM LIGHT/+24V/COM) is a remote command source feeding into this same loop via terminals 17-20, and the SW/ switch cluster (BOOM LTS/COCKPIT LTS/C22) is cross-wired into the V1 valve's terminal 22 per the netlist (net433) though its lighting role is otherwise routed to 690-lts-boom (BOOM LTS) — no clean node exists here for "COCKPIT LTS" as its own item, per q52 flagged on a prior sheet. Supply origin is SALOON COMPANION WAY via breaker Q25 6A, itself off F6 160A from +24V SERVICE BAT, per q53 already flagged as a cross-reference.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Inflatable hatch seal / hatch lock system — AFT Companion Way (575-pneumatic-system)
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Sheet titled AFT COMPANION WAY maps directly per engineer-confirmed vocabulary to 575-pneumatic-system. All hatch-open/closed indicators, the inflation pressure switch, the SW19 selector, the locker inflate/deflate switch, V1/AUX valves and the reed closed-signal switch are the pneumatic seal & hatch-lock control loop for this one companionway.

functions.label: Hatch position indicators S1 (HATCH OPEN) / S2 (HATCH CLOSED)
functions.what_it_does: Two indicator devices report the aft companion-way hatch's open/closed state, fed from the J/BOX relay row (Re3 feeds S1's circuit, Re4 feeds S2's circuit per q47 engineer answer).

flow_scenarios.path: Re3/Re4 relay contacts (via terminals 2 and 3) -> S1 HATCH OPEN indicator and S2 HATCH CLOSED indicator; negative/return side not separately traced on this sheet, positive confirmed by engineer answer q47 as coming through the Re3/Re4 relay row

functions.label: Digital pressure switch — inflation confirmation
functions.what_it_does: Contact-type digital pressure switch that opens when the seal is fully inflated, providing a signal into the J/BOX loop (routed via terminals 4/5) confirming the inflatable gasket state; grounded locally.

flow_scenarios.path: terminal 4/5 loop -> digital pressure switch contact closed -> signal held
terminal 4/5 loop -> digital pressure switch contact opens on inflation -> signal changes state -> switch's other leg returns to earth ground

functions.label: SW19 open/closed/LOCK selector switch
functions.what_it_does: A 3-position (open/closed/LOCK) 6-contact selector switch that commands the hatch/seal function, wired through terminals 6-16 of the J/BOX into the Re1-Re5 relay row (contact=NO for all three functions per the measured netlist), common returned to earth ground.

flow_scenarios.path: SW19 contact 1/2 (NO, open when selected) -> terminal 6/7 -> Re1/Re3 relay row -> hatch open function; common -> earth ground
SW19 contact 3/4 (NO) -> terminal 8/9 -> Re2/Re4 relay row -> hatch closed function; common -> earth ground
SW19 contact 5/6 (NO) -> terminal 10 and 2.7K-tapped terminals 11-16 -> Re5 relay row -> lock function; common -> earth ground

functions.label: Inside-locker inflate/deflate pushbutton
functions.what_it_does: A 2-terminal switch mounted inside the locker lets crew directly command inflate/deflate of the seal, wired via the J/BOX loom into the V1/AUX valve loop.

flow_scenarios.path: SW/ (inside Locker) pin 1/2 -> J/BOX loom -> V1 inflate/deflate valve and/or AUX inflate/deflate valve energised through Re6/Re7/Re8 relay row

functions.label: V1 — INFLATE/DEFLATE valve
functions.what_it_does: Primary pneumatic valve inflating/deflating the companion-way hatch seal, wired from J/BOX terminals 21/22; terminal 22 measured on the same net (net433) as the SW/ (BOOM LTS/COCKPIT LTS/C22) switch's C22 pin, and separately on net471 with the valve body — the exact functional relationship between C22 and V1 is per q49 (engineer notes both companionways have an inflatable seal, and V1/AUX + side comes through the relay row activated by specific functions; the C22 pairing itself is not further resolved on this sheet).

flow_scenarios.path: valve at rest, no current path present
Re6/Re7/Re8 relay row (activated by SW19 LOCK selection or inside-locker SW/ command) -> terminal 21/22 -> V1 valve; return via terminal 22 -> SW/ (BOOM LTS group) C22 pin per net433 measured pairing

functions.dry_data: Positive/feed side of V1 not fully traced on this sheet (per q48 engineer answer: comes through a row of relays activated by specific functions)

functions.label: AUX INFLATE/DEFLATE valve
functions.what_it_does: Secondary/auxiliary pneumatic valve for the same hatch seal, wired from terminal 23; likely a backup or secondary inflation path for the seal per q48 engineer note.

flow_scenarios.path: relay row (per q48, activated by specific functions) -> terminal 23 -> AUX INFLATE/DEFLATE valve

functions.dry_data: Positive/feed side not fully traced on this sheet — per q48 engineer answer, comes through a row of relays activated by specific functions

functions.label: Reed switch — CLOSED SIGNAL
functions.what_it_does: A reed (proximity) switch reports the hatch's closed state as a status signal out via terminal 24, feeding into the wider loop/monitoring.

flow_scenarios.path: reed switch open, no closed-signal asserted
reed switch closes -> terminal 24 -> CLOSED SIGNAL status output

functions.label: Re1-Re8 relay bank — hatch/seal function switching
functions.what_it_does: Eight relays (Re1-Re5 in the upper J/BOX region, Re6-Re8 in the lower region) switch power to the hatch indicators, the SW19-selected functions, and the V1/AUX valves. All SWITCH contacts measured NO with coil=respective relay (Re1/Re2/Re3/Re4/Re5). Re6-Re8 tie together via dotted-line linkages to switch contacts above each coil per the walked loop, forming one interlinked control loop: switch_above_Re7 and switch_above_Re8 both feed forward into Re7/Re8's contact chain, with Re7's contact also driving Re6's coil circuit, and Re8 returning via terminal 25 to earth ground.

flow_scenarios.path: switch_above_Re7 -> Re7 coil feed; Re7 contact (dotted linkage) -> feeds Re8 and switch_above_Re8; Re7 coil return -> Re6 output line; Re8 -> terminal 25 -> earth ground return; Re8 coil also has a feed path from switch_above_Re8

functions.dry_data: All SW/relay contacts on this bank measured NO (normally open) per netlist; Re7/Re8 coil supply/return only partially traced — the dotted-linkage side to switch contacts elsewhere on the sheet is the confirmed path, but the ultimate off-sheet continuation is not resolved

equipment_groups.equipment_name: FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 (remote command source for hatch/seal — cross-referenced, no dedicated node)
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The remote receiver's pinout (open/LOCK/closed/BOOM LIGHT/+24V SUPPLY/COM) feeds terminals 17-20 of the J/BOX serving the same AFT companion-way pneumatic system; it is a remote command input to this system, not a separate piece of equipment with its own register node.

functions.label: FWD Remote Receiver #1 — open/LOCK/closed/BOOM LIGHT remote commands
functions.what_it_does: A remote-control receiver with 7 pins (1=open, 2=LOCK, 3=closed, 4=BOOM LIGHT, 5=unused, 6=+24V SUPPLY, 7=COM) supplies remote open/close/lock commands and a boom-light command into the J/BOX terminal strip (terminals 17-20 connect to pins 4-7 per the sheet's own pin numbering shown, i.e., 17=4/BOOM LIGHT, 18=5, 19=6/+24V SUPPLY [fused terminal], 20=7/COM) — though the exact 1st-to-1st correspondence between receiver pins 1-3 (open/LOCK/closed) and specific J/BOX terminals is NOT separately measured on this sheet.

flow_scenarios.path: FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 pins 1/2/3 -> J/BOX terminal strip (pairing not measured beyond the printed pin list) -> Re-bank functions
FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 pin 6 (+24V SUPPLY) and pin 7 (COM) -> terminal 19 (fused terminal, has built-in replaceable fuse) / terminal 20

infrastructure.system_name: J/BOX # terminal strip and relay enclosure (AFT Companion Way)
facts: Dotted-rectangle enclosure holds terminals numbered 2-25 plus the Re1-Re8 relay bank; this is the wiring hub/junction box for the aft companion-way pneumatic seal system, not a separate piece of equipment.
Terminal 19 has a built-in replaceable fuse (inner rectangle crossed by a line) — a known troubleshooting point on the +24V SUPPLY / receiver pin 6 path.

2.7K resistor callouts appear on the conductors into terminals 12, 13, 14, and 16 — end-of-line resistor values for monitoring loop supervision, exact function/role not detailed further on this sheet.

infrastructure.system_name: +24V DC supply riser (SALOON COMPANION WAY feed)
facts: F6 160A is the main supply fuse from +24V SERVICE BAT feeding downstream to the SALOON COMPANION WAY breaker.
SALOON COMPANION WAY Q25 6A breaker feeds terminal 1 of the J/BOX network on this sheet; this is the incoming supply for the entire AFT COMPANION WAY loop.
This supply riser and its Q25 breaker are shared distribution infrastructure, not part of the pneumatic-system equipment itself.

cross_references.what: to PEDESTAL J/BOX 3 — 5-pin connector (pins 1-5) continuing off-sheet
SALOON COMPANION WAY incoming feed via Q25 6A breaker, and F6 160A fuse from +24V SERVICE BAT
cross_references.referenced_sheet_hint: GMMS 108'-118 (Saloon Companion Way sheet) or +24V DC Distribution sheet

cross_references.what: SW/ (BOOM LTS / COCKPIT LTS / C22) switch cluster — BOOM LTS branch belongs to boom lighting circuit
COCKPIT LTS branch of the same SW/ switch cluster — no dedicated register node identified

good_to_have: Exact 2.7K resistor part/purpose (end-of-line supervision resistors on terminals 12/13/14/16) — value is legible on drawing, functional role not detailed further
F6 160A and Q25 6A are both legible ratings already captured; no further inspection needed
Terminal 19's built-in fuse rating not given on this sheet — capture at inspection if ever needed
FWD Remote Receiver #1 pin 5 appears unused/blank on the printed pinout — confirm at inspection if ever repurposed
uncertainties: The exact terminal-to-pin correspondence between FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 pins 1/2/3 (open/LOCK/closed) and specific J/BOX terminals 17-20 is NOT measured on this sheet — the pinout list and terminal numbers sit close together but no direct netlist pairing is shown for pins 1-3; only pins 4/5 (BOOM LIGHT, net466) are measured as tied to SW/.

The role of the SW/ (BOOM LTS/COCKPIT LTS/C22) switch's C22 terminal, which the netlist ties directly to V1 valve's terminal 22 (net433), versus its BOOM LTS/COCKPIT LTS lighting functions, remains ambiguous per prior engineer note q49 — not re-resolved further by this pass.

Re6, Re7, and Re8 coil positive/negative sides are only partially traceable — the dotted-linkage contacts reach other switch contacts on the sheet, but the ultimate off-sheet source/destination of those linkages (which function selects inflate vs deflate vs lock at V1/AUX) is not fully resolved on this sheet.

Positive/feed side of S1 (HATCH OPEN) and S2 (HATCH CLOSED) indicators, and of V1/AUX INFLATE-DEFLATE valves and the reed switch, is per the ALREADY-ANSWERED engineer notes (q47/q48) understood to come through the Re1-Re5 relay row activated by specific functions — not re-flagging as open, recorded here per rule 10 as resolved not uncertain.
